report.question: What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
report.answer: I have a working garden and am trying to send its location, then move to the next board. Routing actual water and keeping the solar cell facing east while the lamp faces north were worthwhile logical constraints. Repeated JSON framing and repeated unchanged goal summaries felt routine. I also wasted four submissions by omitting the required type field.

report.question: How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?
report.answer: This AI play found the rules coherent and the actual-object versus copied-design distinction useful. I completed landing, ice, twin and arch, then inspected dust and chose to stop before constructing there. I would keep source-dependent effects, simultaneous sky rows, retained record identity, and the arch task where the original garden itself can be the recovered span. Reusing whole assemblies was helpful. I would shorten repeated setup of supports, covers and power links across boards and substantially compress the default command output; the small logical decisions were surrounded by much more JSON and repeated status than I needed. The opening lamp orientation was a meaningful constraint, but later garden and specimen work was increasingly a checklist. Dust looked like another larger combination of already exercised obligations, and I preferred to stop at the clean four-board boundary rather than carry on through six more boards. This is a chosen early stop, not campaign completion or a technical interruption, and describes this AI play rather than measured human enjoyment or duration.
